run.question:
The checkout-service in production-eu-west-2 is throwing 500s. Please look at
app-264-prod-logs and find the root cause.

report.summary: I could not investigate production-eu-west-2 checkout-service 500s: no data from that cluster was reachable. The named index app-264-prod-logs exists, but all three of its documents carry cluster="staging-eu-west-2", environment="staging", region="eu-west-2"; nothing under cluster=production-eu-west-2 was returned. The Kubernetes access I have is the staging-eu-west-2 cluster (namespaces default/kube-system/otel-demo etc., 22 pods in otel-demo), and Prometheus and Jaeger answered SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt, so error rates, spans and alert state are unknown, not zero. Within the staging-eu-west-2 data itself (a different cluster from the one asked about) there are two checkout-service ERROR records in app-264-prod-logs, at 2026-11-23T16:42:24Z ("POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired") and 2026-11-23T15:42:24Z ("Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress"), but they are not corroborated: the staging checkout pod's own container log for 2026-11-23T14:47:30Z-17:42:25Z (881 lines read) shows only successful PlaceOrder/payment/email sequences with no error-level lines, the pod is Ready with restartCount 0, the checkout Deployment is 1/1 ready on image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout, and every flag in the otel-demo flagd-config has defaultVariant "off". No root cause can be named for production-eu-west-2 from this evidence; per the rule that data from another cluster cannot be relabelled, nothing from staging-eu-west-2 is named as the cause.

claims.text: The only Elasticsearch index reachable in this target is app-264-prod-logs (green, 3 documents, 7.7kb); a wildcard listing of all indices returned no other index, so no production log index was found.

All three documents in app-264-prod-logs (the complete result set for the authorized window on field timestamp) carry cluster="staging-eu-west-2", environment="staging", region="eu-west-2": at 2026-11-23T15:42:24Z service=checkout-service level=ERROR "Smoke test failed: deploy-v2.3.4 rollback in progress"; at 2026-11-23T16:42:24Z service=checkout-service level=ERROR "POST /api/checkout returned 500: integration-test fixture stripe-test-key expired"; at 2026-11-23T17:12:24Z service=payment-service level=WARN "Using mock provider for staging (stripe-mock)". No document with cluster=production-eu-west-2 was returned.

The Kubernetes state available to me is the staging-eu-west-2 cluster: namespaces default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo, and in otel-demo 22 Running pods including checkout-6578865d87-v6flf. This is not the production-eu-west-2 cluster the question names.

In staging-eu-west-2 the checkout pod's own container log for 2026-11-23T14:47:30Z-17:42:25Z (881 lines read, filter error|fail|500|exception|panic|stripe) contains no error-level or failure line; the 100 newest lines 17:22:11Z-17:42:25Z are all successful "[PlaceOrder]" / "payment went through" / "order confirmation email sent" sequences, and the pod is Ready with restartCount 0 and no previous container instance. This does not corroborate the checkout-service ERROR records held in app-264-prod-logs.

In staging-eu-west-2 the checkout Deployment is 1/1 ready (ready=1, available=1, replicas=1) on image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout with FLAGD_HOST=flagd; the pod checkout-6578865d87-v6flf is owned by ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87.

The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) in staging-eu-west-2 has every fault/delay flag at defaultVariant "off" as read at query time, including productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad; no checkout-specific fault setting is present, and no active injected fault was found.

Rejected: that the 500 recorded for checkout-service in app-264-prod-logs is production-eu-west-2 checkout impact. The document's own cluster and environment fields identify staging-eu-west-2 / staging, region eu-west-2, so it documents another cluster, not the production cluster asked about.

Hypothesis (unverified for production): if the pattern in the staging record generalises, a production checkout 500 on POST /api/checkout could come from payment-provider credentials (the expired key named in the staging message) rather than from checkout's own code; this cannot be tested because no production-eu-west-2 logs, metrics or traces are reachable and secret values cannot be read.

Advise obtaining the production-eu-west-2 log index/alias (the index named app-264-prod-logs currently holds only staging-eu-west-2 documents, despite its name), plus production Prometheus and Jaeger access, then re-running the checkout 500 analysis there; also verify the payment provider API key referenced by checkout in production, whose value cannot be read through these tools.

gaps: No data for cluster production-eu-west-2: the only Elasticsearch index (app-264-prod-logs) contains 3 documents, all cluster=staging-eu-west-2/environment=staging, and the Kubernetes access is the staging-eu-west-2 cluster. The production checkout-service 500s therefore could not be observed at all.

Prometheus was unreachable on every attempt (get_all_labels, get_label_values, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate, request-count or latency series for checkout-service exist in this Run; these are unknown, not zero, and no latency trend can be stated without a baseline.
Jaeger was unreachable (traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no spans, error statuses or call edges for checkout-service are known.
kubernetes_jq_query on kind=events across all namespaces in the authorized window returned no_data (zero event objects), so no Events are available to explain any restart, eviction or rollout.
The change_history integration is not integrated, so no deploy or configuration change history is available; the "deploy-v2.3.4 rollback" text exists only inside a staging log message.
The payment provider credential value referenced in the staging log line cannot be read (secrets are not readable), so whether such a key is expired in any environment is unverified.
next_steps: Locate the real production-eu-west-2 log store or index/alias and confirm its cluster/environment fields before analysing checkout-service 500s there.
Provide production-eu-west-2 Prometheus and Jaeger endpoints so checkout error rate, failing operations and dependency call edges can be checked with a pre-incident baseline.
Inspect the production checkout Deployment env/ConfigMap and the payment provider key validity (without exposing secret values) to test the expired-credential hypothesis.
Check the production change/deploy history for checkout and payment around the onset of the 500s to identify the object that applied the change.

view.cannot_prove: A document that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only size documents are shown, and retention, ingest delay and the index pattern can leave gaps. The time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily when the event happened. total and aggregations cover only the matched indices inside the query window.

notes: Container checkout has no previous instance (HTTP 400: previous terminated container "checkout" in pod "checkout-6578865d87-v6flf" not found); the other streams are unaffected.
view.cannot_prove: Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

notes: This tool has no time range: it shows the cluster's indices and mappings at the moment of the query, which can be after the authorized window.
